25.explanation: GST was introduced by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016 and rolled out on 1 July 2017.

26.explanation: Under Art. 279A(2)(a) the Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson of the GST Council.

27.explanation: Art. 279A(9): the Centre's vote carries one-third weightage and all States together two-thirds; decisions need a three-fourths majority of weighted votes.

28.explanation: Under the Reverse Charge Mechanism (s.9(3)/(4) CGST Act) the recipient, not the supplier, pays the tax.

29.explanation: The Council is a constitutional body under Art. 279A (not statutory), and its Vice-Chairperson is chosen by the State members from among themselves, so 1 and 2 are wrong. The CBIC Chairperson attends as a permanent, non-voting invitee.

30.explanation: Art. 279A(5) keeps petroleum crude, high-speed diesel, motor spirit (petrol), natural gas and ATF out of GST until the Council recommends a date.

31.explanation: National Emergency has been proclaimed three times: 1962 (China war), 1971 (Indo-Pak war) and 1975 (internal disturbance).

sources.title: Wikipedia: State of emergency in India

32.explanation: Art. 358 automatically suspends Article 19 when an emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression.

33.explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' to prevent misuse of Art. 352 after the 1975 Emergency.

34.explanation: President's Rule in a State is imposed under Article 356.

35.explanation: All three emergencies (Arts. 352, 356, 360) are proclaimed by the President.

36.explanation: Proclamations under Art. 356 and Art. 360 are approved by a simple majority of each House; Art. 352 requires a special majority.

sources.title: Wikipedia: State of emergency in India

37.explanation: In NITI Aayog's EPI 2024 (4th edition, released 14 Jan 2026) Maharashtra ranked first among large states, followed by Tamil Nadu and Gujarat.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Maharashtra tops NITI Aayog's EPI (Jan 2026)

38.explanation: EPI 2024 weights: Business Ecosystem 40%; Export Infrastructure, Policy & Governance and Export Performance 20% each.

39.explanation: EPI classifies states as Leaders, Challengers and Aspirers. 'Achievers' is not a category.

40.explanation: The Export Preparedness Index is prepared and released by NITI Aayog.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Maharashtra tops NITI Aayog's EPI

41.explanation: EPI 2024 is built on 4 pillars split into 13 sub-pillars and 70 indicators.

42.explanation: The UAE announced on 28 April 2026 that it would leave OPEC and OPEC+ with effect from 1 May 2026.

sources.title: WAM: UAE announces decision to exit OPEC & OPEC+

43.explanation: The exit came amid the Iran war and disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

sources.title: Al Jazeera: UAE leaves OPEC in blow to oil cartel during war on Iran (28 Apr 2026)

44.explanation: Saudi Arabia is OPEC's largest producer and its de facto leader.

45.explanation: OPEC has been headquartered in Vienna, Austria since 1965.

46.explanation: OPEC+ (formed in 2016) is OPEC's members plus non-OPEC producers such as Russia. It has no separate headquarters.

47.explanation: Algeria is an OPEC member. India never was, Russia is only in OPEC+, and the UAE left on 1 May 2026.

48.explanation: A 'super' El Niño has much stronger warming, usually Niño-3.4 anomalies around +2°C or more.

49.explanation: The SOI measures the difference in sea-level air pressure between Tahiti and Darwin.

50.explanation: A sustained negative SOI (low Tahiti pressure relative to Darwin) goes with El Niño. A positive SOI goes with La Niña.

51.explanation: La Niña years generally bring normal or above-normal Indian monsoon rainfall. El Niño tends to weaken it.

52.explanation: The south-west monsoon draws its moisture mainly from the Indian Ocean (Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal).
